A1.justification: Both readable, 11-page PDFs describe the same Puzzle Similarity work. Neither includes or embeds the cited supplement. This limits comparison of supplementary analyses and the full-reference results that v2 directs readers to there.

before.justification: V1 reports original human artifact annotations for 36 renderings, metric correlations in Tables 1–3, and inpainting outcomes in Figure 5.

after.justification: V2 reports original human-annotation results, revised and expanded metric comparisons in Tables 1–2, and retained inpainting outcomes in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The cosine-similarity matching, maximum selection, bilinear upsampling, and weighted layer combination remain unchanged. Both use SqueezeNet layers 2–4 with weights 0.67, 0.2, and 0.13, and retain the iterative inpainting procedure. Naming LaMa (big) in v2 discloses an implementation detail without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate 36 renderings from the same twelve scenes drawn from Mip-NeRF360, Tanks and Temples, and Deep Blending. Artifact localization and the garden, kitchen, and flowers inpainting examples remain unchanged. The added comparators introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds CrossScore as the principal cross-reference comparator and adds PaQ-2-PiQ and PAL4VST to the reported no-reference comparisons, retaining CNNIQA and PIQE. Full-reference results are directed to the unavailable supplement, so their absence from v2's tables does not establish that those evaluations were removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported participant count from 23 to 22 without explaining whether this corrects the description or changes participant inclusion. V2 specifies shared training views for CrossScore and bilinear upsampling for new comparator outputs. The 36-image design, correlation metrics, and logistic calibration remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The layer comparison in Figure 3 and inpainting cases in Figure 5 are retained; Figure 4 changes comparator maps on the same scene examples. V2 additionally references supplemental runtime analysis, but the supplement is absent, preventing a reliable assessment of the extent of changes to supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: V1 Table 3 and v2 Table 2 both report means and standard deviations across datasets. Neither supplied PDF adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changed standard-deviation values are result changes; the participant-count revision concerns the evaluation sample.

E6.justification: V2 adds per-scene and aggregate results for three comparators and revises retained scores. PuzzleSim's aggregate Pearson/Spearman values change from 0.592/0.475 to 0.615/0.474; CNNIQA changes from 0.224/0.237 to 0.144/0.130. CrossScore newly scores 0.510/0.378. These are revised or newly reported outcomes, not established same-setting performance gains given the participant-count change.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same similarity definitions, aggregation, logistic calibration, and threshold construction. The assumption about below-average artifact scores and the monotonic PuzzleSim-improvement assertion also remain. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears in the supplied PDFs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion reposition the work within an existing cross-reference category and present the dataset as a benchmark for that category. The comparative claim expands from outperforming no-reference and popular full-reference metrics to state-of-the-art cross-reference artifact localization and superiority over all tested NR, CR, and FR metrics.

C2.justification: V2 interprets lower cross-dataset variability as robustness and attributes CrossScore's limitations to SSIM supervision and its 14-by-14 output blocks. It also newly states that Vision Transformer backbones are unsupported because maintaining a limited receptive field requires special care. Existing computational, resolution, calibration, and gradient limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 names LaMa (big) as the inpainter, specifies bilinear upsampling for CNNIQA, documents handling of new comparators, and adds a project-page link. The dataset footnote remains a placeholder. Detailed full-reference adaptation instructions visible in v1 are instead directed to supplementary material in v2.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands coverage of multimodal, transformer-based, and spatial quality metrics. It newly credits CrossScore with establishing the cross-reference category and makes it the closest comparator, replacing v1's emphasis on PIQE. Added discussion includes PaQ-2-PiQ, PAL4VST, CLIP-based assessment, and SSIM limitations.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution framing, related work, evaluation narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work gains numbered subsections and an expanded metric taxonomy; results are reorganized around evaluation followed by NR, CR, and FR comparisons. Most method and inpainting exposition remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The main comparison displays are substantially restructured: separate per-scene Pearson and Spearman tables become one combined NR/CR table, and the aggregate table is regrouped and reduced. Figure 4 replaces PIQE and FovVideoVDP maps with PaQ-2-PiQ and CrossScore maps. Figures 1–3 and 5 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: Adding CrossScore supplies an important comparison using the same unaligned training views, while clearer cross-reference positioning and broader NR comparisons strengthen the evaluation. Implementation disclosures and the explicit backbone limitation also help. The gain is qualified by unexplained participant-count and score revisions, and by full-reference claims now depending on supplementary evidence absent from the supplied PDFs.
